step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates FPL Technologies' on-demand, serverless machine learning workbench and data lake ingestion pipeline. Data ingestion flows from transactional databases (RDS) through AWS Glue PySpark jobs, which anonymize and transform data before storing domain-specific data marts into an Apache Hudi ACID-compliant S3 data lake. For ML workloads, a Data Scientist (DS) submits Jupyter notebooks (IPYNB) via SageMaker Studio within a private VPC. SageMaker triggers a Lambda function to fetch custom container images (from ECR) containing required dependencies. SageMaker execution is strictly isolated and controlled via IAM execution roles corresponding to specific data science user groups (DS1, DS2). Processed outputs and generated scores are directly saved back into the S3 data lake.

graph.notes: FPL Technologies built an on-demand, serverless ML workbench on AWS using SageMaker Studio, Lambda, Glue, and S3. IAM roles enforce user group workspace isolation while Glue PySpark jobs hydrate an S3 data lake kept ACID compliant via Apache Hudi.

edges.notes: RDS data is funneled into AWS Glue PySpark jobs for ETL transformation.
Glue writes transformed, anonymized data into S3 domain-specific data marts.
Data Scientist logs into SageMaker Studio and submits Jupyter notebooks (IPYNB) for processing jobs.
SageMaker processing job triggers Lambda function to fetch custom execution container image.
SageMaker uses specific IAM execution roles (DS1, DS2) to enforce data access governance and workspace isolation.
Outputs and generated scores from SageMaker processing jobs are dumped into S3 data lake.
